forecast_phases.label: Wave 4 Replacement Authoring + Certification
forecast_phases.qids_note: Covers the final 3 replacement groups. Specific QIDs to be assigned during authoring (R41, R42, R43 in sequence).
forecast_phases.description: Author and certify the 3 remaining replacement items for the final 3 unaddressed replacement groups. Each item requires full stem, 4-choice distractor set, ExplanationCorrect (400+ chars per S311 Quality Gate), 3 ExplanationWrong slots (100+ chars each), LOSTag, Difficulty, CognitiveLevel, and ProductionStatus metadata. Insert into pack_e_corrected.js with ProductionStatus: 'Production', question_state: 'Certified'.
prerequisites: None — all prior waves complete. Wave 2b already done (S808).
deliverables: 3 new replacement items authored and certified
All 43 replacement items now certified (100% replacement program)

risks.description: Only 3 items in 1 session. Wave 1-3 demonstrated steady throughput of 10 items per authoring-certification cycle.
risks.mitigation: Proven methodology; quality gate templates exist; no new tooling required.

forecast_phases.label: Seed Certification Phase 1 (P1 — Higher Priority)
forecast_phases.description: Certify the first ~19 seed items (prioritized by blueprint coverage criticality and EW gap severity). Each seed requires: (a) EW gap fill — author choice-specific ExplanationWrong for ~38 empty slots, minimum 100 chars per S311 Quality Gate; (b) EC expansion — expand ExplanationCorrect from 80-120 chars to 400+ chars with COSO principle citations and business interpretation; (c) stem/distractor rewrite for CMA-style application-level scenarios; (d) LOSTag recalibration from coarse 'E Internal controls' to fine-grained E.1.a–E.1.i sub-tags; (e) DL-031 difficulty/CognitiveLevel recalibration; (f) ProductionStatus set to 'Draft' before entering pipeline; (g) CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification and quality gate review.
prerequisites: Cross-reference audit: verify Pack C vs Pack D seeds do not duplicate each other (same concept, different company name)
EW gap ledger per seed — enumerate which EW slots are empty per item
deliverables: ~19 seeds fully remediated and CAQS §1.6 certified
EC expanded to 400+ chars per seed

risks.description: All 38 seeds score 1-3/10 on EC adequacy, EW completeness, stem quality, distractor quality, and LOSTag precision per SESSION318_SEED_INVENTORY.json. Remediation effort of 1.5-2.5 hrs/seed is estimated but unvalidated at scale.
risks.mitigation: Pilot the first 5 seeds to calibrate actual per-item effort before committing to full Phase 2 schedule. If per-item effort exceeds 2.5 hrs, re-baseline the Phase 2/3 split.

risks.description: Pack C and Pack D seeds may be symmetric clones (same concept, different company name, rotated CC letter). Certifying both would create duplicate coverage.
risks.mitigation: Mandatory cross-reference audit before Phase 2 start (1 session). If duplication confirmed, consolidate to ~19 unique seeds across both packs, reducing Phase 2+3 combined workload from 38 to ~19.

forecast_phases.label: Seed Certification Phase 2 (P2 — Standard Priority)
forecast_phases.description: Certify the remaining ~19 seed items. Same remediation pipeline as Phase 2: EW gap fill, EC expansion, stem/distractor rewrite, LOSTag recalibration, DL-031 calibration, ProductionStatus assignment, and CAQS §1.6 certification. Lessons learned from Phase 2 should reduce per-item effort through template reuse and streamlined review.
prerequisites: Refined effort model from Phase 2 actuals
deliverables: ~19 seeds fully remediated and CAQS §1.6 certified
All 38 Pack C/D Domain E seeds certified
EW gap reduced by remaining ~38 slots

risks.description: Phase 3 depends on Phase 2 completing on schedule. Any Phase 2 overrun cascades into Phase 3. Combined Phase 2+3 budget of 7 sessions is tight for 38 items at 1.5-2.5 hrs/item.
risks.mitigation: Phase 2 actuals inform Phase 3 rebaseline. If Phase 2 takes 4 sessions, adjust Phase 3 to 4 sessions (S324-S327) and push closure to S328.

risks.description: Later seeds may cover narrower/more esoteric E.1 sub-topics where Pack B benchmark coverage is thinner, making quality targets harder to meet.
risks.mitigation: Accept that some niche sub-topics may certify at the S311 minimum bar (400 chars EC, 100 chars EW) rather than the aspirational Pack A seed bar (923 chars EC). Document any such decisions in the certification record.

forecast_phases.label: Domain E Closure and Final Count
forecast_phases.description: Final reconciliation and governance closure for Domain E modernization program. Verify all 81 modernization items are certified and inserted. Reconcile Domain E certification count (238 baseline + 81 modernization = 319). Update Portfolio Certification Dashboard. Publish Domain E Closure Report. Conduct governance attestation with all 5 quality gates verified across all waves and seed phases.
deliverables: All 5 quality gates verified across full modernization program
Domain E UIQS final score and grade

risks.description: Registry entries across MQR, QSL, and DPR may have accumulated inconsistencies across 4 phases and multiple insertion events.
risks.mitigation: Run full cross-registry reconciliation in S327 before attestation. Any gaps are data-entry issues, not structural defects.

domain_e_certification.delta_note: 238 (current Domain E certified, confirmed by S808) + 81 modernization items (43 replacements + 38 seeds) = 319. The 40 already-inserted replacement items are counted in the 238 baseline; the remaining 41 net-new certifications (3 Wave 4 authoring + 38 seed certifications) plus the 40 already counted = 81 total modernization items contributing to the Domain E count.

portfolio_certification.gap_note: Remaining 198 uncertified items are outside Domain E scope (Packs A-D other domains, case-bank items, etc.). Domain E modernization alone does not close the full portfolio gap.

domain_e_uiqs_projection.note: Per S312 projection model. Domain E UIQS will decline from 90.0 (replacement-only average) to ~77.1 when legacy seeds at lower quality (estimated 55-65 UIQS each) are included in the Domain E average. This is expected: replacement items are high-quality new content (88-93 range) while seeds are remediated legacy content.

external_dependencies.description: All seed certifications must pass the six-dimension CAQS §1.6 verification. If the standard is revised or tightened mid-program, previously certified seeds may need re-validation.
EC 400+ chars, EW 100+ chars per slot thresholds are the minimum bar. If the gate is raised (e.g., EC 600+), seed remediation effort increases proportionally.
external_dependencies.impact_if_failed: Each +100 chars EC adds ~0.25 hrs/seed (9.5 hrs across 38 seeds).

external_dependencies.description: Pack B (75/75 Certified) is the quality target for LOSTag distribution, EC depth, EW instructional value, and distractor plausibility. Any degradation of Pack B as a benchmark (e.g., re-audit finding defects) would invalidate the quality target.
external_dependencies.impact_if_failed: Low probability; Pack B is the gold standard and has been stable across multiple audits.

internal_dependencies: Master Question Registry (MQR) — must accept 41 new rows across all phases (3 replacement + 38 seeds)
Question Similarity Ledger (QSL) — must accept 41 new entries, no collision with existing QIDs
Duplicate Prevention Report (DPR) — Gate 0 must pass for every insertion batch
pack_e_corrected.js — must remain parseable and syntactically valid through multiple insertion events (currently 540 → 543 → 562 → 581)

risk_register.confidence_rationale: The Wave 4 replacement authoring (Phase 1) is LOW risk — only 3 items, methodology proven across 4 waves, quality gates stable. However, the seed certification phases (Phases 2-3) represent the largest variable: 38 legacy items with 1-3/10 readiness scores across all quality dimensions. Per-item remediation effort of 1.5-2.5 hours is an estimate, not an actual. If actual effort trends toward 3+ hrs/seed, Phase 2+3 combined could require 9-10 sessions instead of 7, pushing closure from S327 to S329-S330.

top_risks.impact: Phase 2+3 sessions increase from 7 to 9-10; Domain E closure slips from S327 to S329-S330; portfolio certification delayed by 2-3 sessions.
top_risks.trigger: Phase 2 first 5 seeds exceed 2.5 hrs/item average.
top_risks.contingency: Re-baseline after first 5 seeds. If trend is 3+ hrs/seed, reduce Phase 2 batch size to 15 items (S320-S324) and Phase 3 to 15 items (S325-S329), with closure at S330.

top_risks.impact: If Pack C and Pack D seeds are symmetric clones (same concept, different company name), certifying both wastes 19 certifications on duplicate coverage.
top_risks.contingency: This is actually a positive outcome — it reduces the seed workload from 38 to ~19 items, saving 3-4 sessions. The forecast already builds in the cross-reference audit as a Phase 2 prerequisite.

top_risks.impact: MQR, QSL, and DPR may accumulate inconsistencies across 4 phases and multiple insertion events. Reconciliation in S327 catches these.
top_risks.trigger: Cross-registry row counts diverge from expected values.
top_risks.contingency: Standard reconciliation procedure; no session impact beyond S327 closure work.

top_risks.impact: If CAQS §1.6 or S311 Quality Gate thresholds are raised mid-program, previously certified items may need re-validation.
top_risks.trigger: New governance directive or audit finding.
top_risks.contingency: Grandfather existing certifications; apply new standard only to uncertified items. Document decision in governance log.

Per-seed remediation effort of 1.5-2.5 hours holds at scale. Pilot of first 5 seeds in Phase 2 will validate or rebaseline.
Cross-reference audit (Phase 2 prerequisite) may reduce seed workload from 38 to ~19 if Pack C/D symmetry is confirmed. This forecast conservatively assumes all 38 seeds require certification.
No new DL defects are discovered in Pack C/D Domain E seeds beyond those already documented (DL-008 clean, DL-013 partial, DL-026 partial, DL-031 uncalibrated).
Pack B Section E (75/75 Certified) remains the stable quality benchmark throughout the forecast period.
No external schedule interruptions (e.g., platform migration, tooling changes, governance freezes) during S319-S327.
